release_notes: The PHP patch command from the security banner is now paste-safe. Pasting the v1.7.6 block as a whole died at apt's "Continue? [Y/n]" — the next pasted line (systemctl…) was read as the answer, apt aborted, and the upgrade never ran even though the resolution was correct. The banner now prints: apt update, then "NEEDRESTART_MODE=a apt install -y --only-upgrade 'php8.X-*'" (your branch), then "systemctl restart php8.X-fpm nginx", then php -v — no interactive prompts anywhere: -y answers the confirmation, NEEDRESTART_MODE=a answers the Ubuntu 22.04+ "which services to restart" dialog that would otherwise swallow the restart line. The advisory is unchanged: CVE-2026-109618 / CVE-2026-109619 ("php2shell") are unauthenticated RCE bugs in PHP itself with a public exploit; fixed releases are 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 and 8.2.35, and PHP 8.1 or older will never get one (re-run "sudo bash install.sh" to move to PHP 8.5). Distro builds may carry the fix backported under the old version number: apt changelog php-fpm | grep 109618.
